recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5837 unless the work group separately wants an editorial cleanup of the `Information  Suppressed` display spacing.
issue_request: FHIR-5837 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core OperationOutcome and asked to add warning-oriented IssueType codes: `suppressed` under Security, `incomplete` under Processing, and `informational` as a top-level category.
initial_application: The Jira resolution records an SVN application, and git-svn commit 97a8b1d95b (`#5837 - improvements to Issue-Type code system`) updated the old OperationOutcome spreadsheet to revise `suppressed`, add `incomplete`, add `informational`, and improve IssueType definitions.
additional_context: OperationOutcome is active in `source/fhir.ini`, and the current authoritative terminology file is `source/operationoutcome/codesystem-issue-type.xml`. It contains all three requested codes. The only substantive difference from the original request is that `incomplete` now sits under `transient`; later Published issue FHIR-17329 and commit e1337d4063 explain that current categorization as later applied IssueType work.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current CodeSystem preserves the FHIR-5837 additions, and changing the later hierarchy or making display-only spacing edits would not improve current conformance semantics.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive-with-Modification OperationOutcome IssueType work added API-related missing codes and moved `incomplete` under `transient`, explaining the current hierarchy.

Later OperationOutcome modeling kept `issue.code` as a required base code and moved more-specific coding to details, reinforcing why the IssueType list matters but not requiring a separate decision here.
